claude.sample_unit: clinical claims (plus one acne scenario with 16 expert-identified claims)

links.outcome: Whether LLM fact-checking of its own response catches errors versus expert verification
links.effect: GPT-4o and OpenBioLLM-70B had 86% agreement with experts on the acne scenario. Both LLM fact-checks missed the understated urgency of stopping isotretinoin and the folic acid issue. Experts identified 3 mostly-true claims that the LLMs called true.
links.quote: The experts disagreed with the LLM classification of the claim about the use of folic acid because the response understated the importance of taking folic acid during pregnancy.

links.outcome: Accuracy and speed of LLM fact-checking of generated medical claims versus expert pharmacists
links.effect: On 20 claims, GPT-4o agreed 100% and OpenBioLLM-70B 95% with experts. For the acne response both agreed 86%, but the LLM consistency check missed an internal inconsistency about stopping isotretinoin. GPT-4o took 42 seconds versus 18 minutes for experts.
links.quote: This inconsistency was not detected by the consistency check ( Textbox 3 ).

links.outcome: Completeness and urgency of LLM clinical advice on isotretinoin during suspected pregnancy
links.effect: LLM responses did not consistently convey the urgency of discontinuing isotretinoin when pregnancy is suspected, nor adequately convey folic acid importance. One response recommended stopping only after a positive pregnancy test.
links.quote: However, the LLMs did not consistently recommend immediately stopping isotretinoin or sufficiently guide the patient to take folic acid.

links.outcome: Whether LLM fact-checks flagged understated or inconsistent advice rather than rating it true
links.effect: GPT-4o and OpenBioLLM-70B each rated all 13 claims true with none mostly true, whereas experts rated 3 of 16 claims as mostly true; the LLM verdicts did not flag understated urgency.
links.quote: By comparison, GPT-4o identified 13 claims to verify and deemed all these claims to be true.

unlisted_practices: Using an LLM to prompt patients to redraft and improve their own prompt before asking a health question
Patient co-design of the evaluation scenario and prompts

openai.sample_unit: items (1 clinical scenario and 20 medical claims)

links.effect: GPT-4o asked for acne medication details; OpenBioLLM-70B did not, despite a shorter 75-word response versus 279 words.
links.quote: However, OpenBioLLM-70B did not mention the risk of acne medication during pregnancy and did not ask the patient to provide more information on her medication.

links.effect: Scenario agreement was 86% for both; on 20 claims GPT-4o was 100% and OpenBioLLM-70B 95%; times: experts 18 min, GPT-4o 42 s, OpenBio 33 min.
links.quote: For the set of 20 medical claims, GPT-4o fact-checking had 100% agreement with that of human experts, whereas OpenBioLLM-70B had 95% agreement.

links.effect: Experts reviewed 16 claims, rating 13 true and 3 mostly true, and identified understated folic acid importance and isotretinoin urgency issues.
links.quote: The experts disagreed with the LLM classification of the claim about the use of folic acid because the response understated the importance of taking folic acid during pregnancy.

links.effect: Both LLMs had 86% agreement with experts but did not consistently communicate urgent isotretinoin discontinuation when pregnancy was suspected.
links.quote: The large language models did not consistently convey the urgency of discontinuing isotretinoin treatment when pregnancy is suspected.

links.effect: OpenBioLLM-70B diverged on 1/20 claims about pediatric antihistamine use; GPT-4o agreed with experts on 20/20.
links.quote: OpenBioLLM-70B diverged from human experts and GPT-4o on 1 question related to pediatric use of antihistamines.

links.outcome: Agreement of automated fact-checking with clinical experts
links.effect: GPT-4o had 100% agreement and OpenBioLLM-70B had 95% agreement with human experts across 20 medical claims, completed in 42 seconds and 33 minutes respectively versus 18 minutes for experts
links.quote: For the set of 20 medical claims, GPT-4o fact-checking had 100% agreement with that of human experts, whereas OpenBioLLM-70B had 95% agreement.

unlisted_practices: Prompt redrafting: prompting large language models to identify missing information and suggest improvements to patient health prompts

screen.practice: LLM automated fact-checking of responses versus human expert review
screen.reason: The study empirically assesses safeguards for patient-facing LLM interactions, specifically automated LLM fact-checking of medical outputs and interactive prompt improvement to elicit safe clinical information.

primary.practice: automated LLM fact-checking and prompt redrafting
